Posted May 1, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan
See
Walters Puts The Media to the Test By Taking Hyper-Lying to A New Level. Blood Libels To Justify Police State. San Diego Medical Activist Faces Federal Charges for 20 Plants.

The outrageous federal prosecution of San Diego medical cannabis activist Steve McWilliams for just 25 plants shows that medical cannabis is a political crime and defendants cannot get a fair trial in federal courts. This is a tragedy for McWilliams, and an important message to Immigration Canada about the fate that would befall the medical refugees if they are sent back.

On April 28th,Steve McWilliams was sentenced to six months in federal prison for growing 25 marijuana plants in his front yard. He was certainly up front about it.

Because he would not be allowed even to mention anything about medical cannabis or his own medical condition in a federal court, he had no choice but to plead guilty on February 7th to one federal count of aiding and abetting, and manufacturing marijuana.

Although he will remain free pending his appeal, U.S. District Judge James Fitzpatrick ordered him not to use cannabis as a condition of release while the case is appealed. In stead, he will be forced to use more powerful and debilitating pharmaceuticals, and the incredibly expensive Marinol, which does not work as well. All of this places a great financial burden on his family.
See
Why Marinol Is Not Medical Marijuana
and
A Medical Marijuana User Says That " Marinol Rescheduling Is Worthless " For Him. He Simply Cannot Afford It. " My country is killing me. "

This is standard for everyone on federal bail or probation. In fact, this reminds me of the fed's treatment of the late Peter McWilliams. (no kin)
See
 " The federal prosecutor personally called my mother to tell her that if I was found with even a trace of medical marijuana, her house would be taken away. " -- Peter McWilliams

And, of course, if he loses his appeal, he would serve six months in federal prison without the use of medical cannabis, and probably would not even be allowed to use Marinol. After that he will also have to serve three years probation, during which he will be subjected to regular urine testing to be sure that he is not using the plant.

Steve said, " I think it's torture. I think it's inhumane. When you're in prison, you don't get medical treatment. "

McWilliams, who uses cannabis to relieve chronic pain from injuries suffered in automobile and motorcycle accidents, distributed medical cannabis to sick people in front of San Diego City Hall last year.

Threatening letters from the Feds:

A DEA agent approached him on the street a week later and handed him a letter warning him to stop cultivating his plants or face arrest. McWilliams was arrested last Oct. 11, three weeks after members of the San Diego Narcotics Task Force seized the plants from in front of his home.

In other words, being a visible activist warrants federal prosecution, no matter how few plants are involved. The B. E. Smith case involved only 87 plants.
See
Smith Sentenced to 27 Months In Federal Prison For 87 Medical Marijuana Plants:
Judge Cites Smith's " Disdain For Federal Law " What Is The Definition Of A " Political Prisoner? " "Every day I m in prison will be seen by me as another day in service of my nation. " " I forgive you for what you're about to do to me. "

The only reason that he is being allowed to remain free on appeal is that there are several related cases in the 9th Circuit challenging the Federal interference with the state's medical cannabis laws. It could be well over a year before all these cases make it to the Supreme Court.

What makes this case even more obviously political is that McWilliams had been working with the San Diego City Council, which recently voted to accept guidelines that allow sick people to have up to a pound of medical cannabis.
See
San Diego Medical Cannabis Activists/Providers Resume Providing Patients with Medicine; Believe It or Not: Meeting with Chief of Police at 4:20 Today.

McWilliams was one of the original members of the city's Medical Cannabis Task Force, and he even had letters of commendation from the Mayor of San Diego, but the federal judge would not even listen to any evidence, because it is irrelevant under federal law.

" We think that the sentencing was very unfair. It doesn't respect the rights of seriously ill Californians to obey California state law. The city council approved guidelines which explicitly condone and sanction the exact same conduct for which I was just sentenced. We think the U.S. Attorney's Office is trying to squash our state initiatives by using our patients as pawns, " McWilliams said.

In other words, being outspoken like Kubby and Tuck, or providing medical cannabis with local approval, like Tuck and Hayes, makes a person a federal target no matter how few plants a person has. Of course, all of them had far more plants than McWilliams. It is quite clear that they would not be safe if they had to leave Canada.
See
Placer County: Still Crazy After All These Years. Kubby Hearings Offer New Evidence California Law Enforcement Still Fighting Medical Cannabis Law. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com
and
Reading Between The Lies. New Version of An Old Lie About My Saying Medical Cannabis Is A Scam May Be Clue to New Prohibitionist Party Line. Only A Few Hundred Patients?
and
In Their Own Words: FDA Press Release On New Anti-Nausea Drug For Chemotherapy Patients Prove Prohibitionists Are Lying About Need For Medical Cannabis.
